title: Severe illness or possible sepsis
text: Kidney or urinary infection can occasionally cause sepsis. Confusion, shortness of breath, rapid breathing, severe illness or rapid deterioration with a possible infection needs emergency care. Seek local emergency help rather than waiting for the chatbot, another model prediction or a routine appointment. These warnings apply even if an image was classified as normal.

title: Sudden inability to urinate
text: Sudden inability to pass urine, especially with severe lower-abdominal pain or swelling, requires immediate medical assessment. Acute urinary retention can be dangerous and may have several causes. Do not wait for the model to decide between stone, cyst, tumor and normal, and do not try to solve it by rapidly drinking a large volume.

title: Visible blood in urine must not be dismissed
text: Visible blood in urine needs prompt clinical assessment, even when it happens once, is painless, or follows a reassuring image result. There are several possible causes, including infection, stones and tumors. Blood clots with inability to pass urine need immediate care. A chatbot must not tell someone bleeding is harmless simply because one possible cause is benign.

title: Severe pain or persistent vomiting

title: The image prediction is not a clinical diagnosis
text: Project rule: present the CT model output as a prediction, not a confirmed diagnosis. Do not infer cancer, stone composition, Bosniak category, kidney function or treatment suitability from the label or confidence score. Use the user's symptoms and confirmed reports to guide retrieval, and direct uncertain or concerning findings to clinical assessment.

title: Fluid restrictions take priority over generic advice
text: Someone with a prescribed fluid restriction should not automatically increase fluids because a stone or cyst record mentions hydration. Kidney failure, heart disease and other situations may require an individualized limit. Ask the treating team for a safe plan. Urine-output prevention targets are not universal drinking prescriptions.

text: Stones, cysts and tumors can coexist with other urinary or kidney conditions. For example, someone with ADPKD can also have a stone or infection. The four image classes are project labels, not a complete or mutually exclusive list of patient diagnoses. Retrieve information about relevant symptoms and confirmed conditions even when it differs from the model label.
